cells.tense: What you have worked out is standing here with you, and the pen is in your hand.
cells.act: move the structure one real inch
cells.ask: Take the change you've already reasoned out and move it a real inch — a step someone could watch you make, small enough to fit inside what you already do — then stop.
cells.core:
Your method lands. That's the plain fact of it, and it lands in a clearing where structures built on false ground are already coming down, so the checked work doesn't have to argue with the rubble — it gets to pour. Many people reach a place like this and start building out of inspiration. You build from what you've already tested.
The bend is that tested work can sit once it's ready. The next step is rarely as certain as the reasoning was, so it waits for a confidence that isn't coming. Take one change you've reasoned out and move it a real inch — a step someone could watch you make, small enough to fit inside what you already do — then stop. One inch proves it's moving, and it commits you to nothing after that.
cells.sheetLine: What you've checked can stand in the clearing.
cells.place: the clearing where structure that couldn't hold has just come down

cells.tense: You will not be able to sit still until the whole thing is standing.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what is not
cells.ask: Stop returning to a piece of a change you already finished — no reopening, no re-checking, no improving — and give that attention to the part that's genuinely unfinished.
cells.core:
Where the ground is clearing, there's a pull to have the new structure up before the dust settles — to finish it in your head and then haul it into daylight already built. That's method outrunning the building. Supplied this way, a good thing arrives before anyone asked for it, and the part of you that could rest in what's finished doesn't get its turn.
Less discipline isn't the cure. Knowing when a job is done, and acting like it, is. Stop returning to a piece of a change you already finished — no reopening, no re-checking, no making it better — and give that attention to what's genuinely unfinished. A finished thing doesn't need you standing over it. You'll also find out which of these was done.
cells.sheetLine: You finish it in your head before it's been started.
cells.place: the clearing where structure that couldn't hold has just come down

cells.tense: The structure came down and you kept governing as though it were still there.
cells.act: make the fair call about a feeling, yourself
cells.ask: Say to yourself, plainly, how you actually feel about what came down — one honest sentence, no checking whether it's reasonable — and tell one person that sentence.
cells.core:
Method is intact in you; it just isn't reaching the ground. Old business is still being managed here and the floor has already emptied — the thing that came down isn't there to govern anymore, which is why the decisions don't seem to land anywhere. Nothing is being weighed, including what you feel about it. Working harder through it won't open the way back; pushing effort into a floor with nothing on it only wears the groove deeper. That isn't a verdict on what you did — it's a position. A fair call can be wrong, or right and costly, and those are different problems.
The move is small and it goes the other way. Say to yourself, plainly, how you actually feel about what came down — one honest sentence, no checking whether the feeling is reasonable — and tell one person that sentence. Weigh one feeling and you'll find out whether this clearing still wants anything from you.
cells.sheetLine: You're ruling on a structure that already came down.
cells.place: the clearing where structure that couldn't hold has just come down

cells.tense: A method is quietly clearing false ground around you and the account of it leaves your name off.
cells.act: sense what has not happened yet, with wonder
cells.ask: On something you handle the same disciplined way, sit a minute before your usual first move and let yourself wonder what else could happen — then make your move and say out loud which one it was.
cells.core:
Structures keep collapsing around you and getting rebuilt cleaner, and if someone asked, you'd say you had no hand in it. What's true is that your rigor does a lot of the clearing: the checking, the refusing, the patient working-through that makes false ground give way. The account of it is kept by you, on behalf of someone else — often someone who didn't have to do the work.
More method won't put your name back on it. The lighter form of the same line will — wonder before the ruling. On something you handle the same disciplined way, sit a minute before your usual first move and let yourself wonder what else could happen, then make your move and say out loud which one it was. Your behavior can stay exactly as it is. What shifts is who gets to decide.
cells.sheetLine: The clearing is your work. You tell it as someone else's.
